title: Aid’s Next Chapter
gist: Foreign aid is shrinking, not disappearing: OECD donors still disbursed $174.3 billion in 2025 after the sharpest annual decline on record, including $29 billion from the US even after the Trump administration cut 83% of USAID programs. The open question is what aid architecture emerges from the retrenchment, not whether rich countries keep spending abroad.

insights.claim: OECD donors provided $174.3 billion in assistance in 2025 even after the sharpest annual decline on record, showing the aid system contracted rather than collapsed.
insights.speaker: NANCY QIAN
insights.so_what: Sizes the residual market for NGOs, development contractors, and recipient-country budgets after the 2025 cuts — a smaller but still $170bn+ pool.
insights.quote: Even after the sharpest annual decline on record, OECD donors still provided $174.3 billion in assistance in 2025.

insights.claim: The United States still contributed $29 billion of 2025 aid despite the Trump administration slashing 83% of USAID programs.
insights.speaker: NANCY QIAN
insights.so_what: Quantifies the floor under US aid: even an 83% program cut leaves a substantial disbursement base, so 'zero US aid' scenarios for recipient sovereigns are overstated.
insights.quote: This includes $29 billion from the United States, despite the slashing of 83% of US Agency for International Development (USAID) programs by Donald Trump’s administration.
insights.locator: CHICAGO—Foreign aid is shrinking, but it is not disappearing

insights.claim: Wars, epidemics, displacement, and geopolitical competition will ensure rich countries keep spending abroad, whether for humanitarian reasons or self-interest.
insights.speaker: NANCY QIAN
insights.so_what: Aid flows should be modeled as structurally persistent but reallocated toward strategic and crisis spending rather than long-horizon development.
insights.quote: wars, epidemics, displacement, and geopolitical competition will ensure that rich countries continue to spend money abroad

insights.claim: The relevant question is what sort of aid system emerges from the current retrenchment — the delivery architecture, not the headline volume, is what will change.
insights.speaker: NANCY QIAN
insights.so_what: Shifts the watch item from aid budgets to delivery channels: which implementers, multilaterals, and bilateral vehicles capture the reshaped flows.
insights.quote: The only question is what sort of aid system will emerge from the current retrenchment.
insights.locator: Wars, epidemics, displacement, and geopolitical competition
